subject: Re: Amendment request — realignment of committed usage & invoice credits
messages:
From: Emma Locke <emma.locke@neurolytics.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neurolytics.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Amendment proposal — committed usage rebalance + invoice credit

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As discussed, Neurolytics is looking to realign our committed usage to reflect shifting workload patterns — specifically, moving 30% of our reserved throughput from Q3 to Q4 and applying a one-time invoice credit for unused commitment in Q2.

Attached is a draft amendment that (a) reduces committed units for the remaining Q3 months, (b) adds a usage-credit line that nets against the next invoice, and (c) reorders Exhibit B pricing tiers so our effective per-token rate in Q4 is lowered.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept retroactive credit for the April–June period (our preference), or alternatively apply the credit forward across the next six invoices? We would like to lock in language this month so we can finalize internal approvals.

Files attached: Neurolytics_Draft_Amendment_v1.docx (redline + supporting schedule)

Proposed timeline: legal review this week -> commercial approval next week -> signature by 8/24.

Thanks,
Emma Locke
Head of Procurement
Neurolytics Inc.

Date: 2026-08-13T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Amendment proposal — committed usage rebalance + invoice credit

Hi Emma — thanks for sending this over and for the timeline. I looped in Kar (sales) and Markus (legal) and Priyom for SOW alignment. A few quick items we need clarified before legal redlines: 

- Which Exhibit(s) should reflect the moved capacity? Is this a net transfer across SKU lines or a one-time top-up/top-down? The draft seems to adjust both Exhibit A and Exhibit B.
- For the invoice credit: is Neurolytics asking for a retroactive cash credit for Q2 usage shortfall, or a credit applied to future invoices? Your email mentions both options; please indicate preferred fallback.
- Do you need any changes to the termination / refund wording (e.g., pro rata refunds vs. one-time credits)?

Markus — if you can review the attached draft and call out any deal-breakers (export control, audit log obligations, termination exposure) that would be great. Priyom, can you confirm the implementation window if we accept the Q4 reallocation?

Happy to set up a 30-minute legal + commercial sync tomorrow afternoon if that helps accelerate.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Emma Locke <emma.locke@neurolytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Amendment proposal — committed usage rebalance + invoice credit

Laura / team,

I reviewed Neurolytics_Draft_Amendment_v1 and prepared a redline with commentary (attached). Summary of material items from legal: 

1) Retroactive credit: We are open to a credit but cannot make it "cash-back" for services rendered more than 60 days prior to the amendment effective date. We propose a credit applied to future invoices spread over 3 billing cycles (language in §2.3).

2) Termination / refunds: Current MSA has pro rata termination for reserved capacity; proposed amendment must not expand Redwood's liability. Suggested language: maintain existing pro rata refund mechanism and add a short clause clarifying that reallocated units are non-refundable once used.

3) Effective date & scope: Redline sets effective date to the signature date and ties Exhibit updates to an "Exhibit Change Order" that both parties sign, to avoid unilateral mid-quarter reassignments.

4) Export controls & data residency: Add a one-sentence warranty (standard) and require Neurolytics to notify Redwood if any data is subject to additional export restrictions.

5) Pricing recalculation: The draft's formula for per-unit reprice had a rounding discrepancy that could lower effective revenue per unit; I corrected the formula in the redline. Please ask the customer to confirm the target effective per-token rate.

I attached RDW_Amendment_Redline_v1.docx with tracked changes and inline comments. I recommend we ask for a short call to resolve the retro credit cadence and the Exhibit-change gating language.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: RDW_Amendment_Redline_v1.docx (docx, 52KB)

From: Emma Locke <emma.locke@neurolytics.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neurolytics.com, Rajiv Menon <cfo@neurolytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Amendment proposal — committed usage rebalance + invoice credit

Markus / Laura,

Appreciate the fast review and the redline. A few quick responses from our side: 

- Credit mechanism: Neurolytics prefers a forward-applied credit spread over 6 invoices to preserve cash flow predictability; we understand Redwood's 60-day lookback limitation. Would you accept 6 invoices instead of 3?
- Effective date: We can accept signature-date effective, but we need Exhibit updates to be backdated to the start of Q3 for internal accounting accuracy if credit is applied retroactively. If your legal position prevents backdating, we can work with forward credits only.
- Pricing math: Rajiv flagged the rounding change Markus made. We need to understand the net effective per-token rate post-adjustment; could you provide a worked example showing the original vs. corrected formula across the proposed reallocation?

I've attached our internal approved redlines to speed negotiation (we left your suggested export control line as-is). If we can settle the credit cadence and either accept forward-only credit or agree a limited backdate (no earlier than 6/1/2026), we can route for signature.

Thanks,
Emma Locke
Head of Procurement
Neurolytics Inc.

Date: 2026-08-16T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Amendment proposal — committed usage rebalance + invoice credit

Emma — thanks for the clear responses and for the approved redline. Quick summary / next steps: 

- Credit cadence: Redwood can accept application of the credit across 6 invoices (agreed — Markus confirmed legal flexibility for a longer amortization window). I will update §2.3 to reflect six invoice spread.
- Backdating: We cannot backdate the Exhibit to an earlier effective date, but we will include an accounting statement in Exhibit C that documents the Q2 shortfall and schedules the six-invoice credit so your accounting team has a clear reconciliation artifact.
- Worked example: Priyom will draft a short worked-pricing example showing original vs. corrected formulas and the expected effective per-token rates post-rebalance and circulate by EOD tomorrow.

If those points are acceptable, Markus and I will prepare a clean amendment incorporating: revised §2.3 (6-invoice credit), Exhibit C reconciliation language, and the corrected pricing formula. We will then send to DocuSign for signatures (targeting signature by 8/24).

Would you be available for a 20-minute call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to confirm wording and sign-off? If yes, I will send calendar invite.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
